The researchers conducted an interview and reviewed the existing incident recording procedure of the client to gather important information about the current manual process. The collected information helped identify how reports are received, assessed, recorded, reviewed, signed, logged, and compiled. This provided a clearer understanding of the client’s current technical situation and served as the basis for identifying the requirements needed for the proposed syst

The Crime Incident Recording Process begins when the complainant reports a crime incident to the Desk Officer through a walk-in complaint. The Desk Officer receives and assesses the report, then forwards it to the Duty Investigator. The Duty Investigator manually fills out the CIRAS form and reviews the details with the complainant. Once the information is verified, the complainant signs the IRF, after which the Desk Officer logs the record and the Crime Registrar compiles it for UCPER.

The Non-Crime Incident Recording Process begins when the complainant reports a non-crime incident to the Desk Officer through a walk-in complaint. The Desk Officer receives and assesses the report, then forwards it to the Police Officer. The Police Officer manually fills out the Incident Record Form and reviews the details with the complainant. After the complainant signs the IRF, the Desk Officer logs the incident into the Police Blotter
